questionsToConsider: Which editing is allowed in your contest, and is the line between basic adjustments and compositing clear to entrants?
Do you accept entries from under-18s, and what does a guardian need to agree to?
How many photos may each person enter, in total and per category?
What rights do you need to show winning photos, and for how long?
guide.howToUseResponses: Export the entries to CSV and filter by category, so each group of judges only sees their own section. Hide the entrant columns before judging if you want scoring to be blind. Email guardians of under-18 entrants to confirm before a photo goes on the shortlist, and check the editing answer again when you look at the full resolution file of any winner.
customizeSteps: Replace the categories with your own, and add the closing date to the greeting.
Rewrite the entry terms to match your contest rules and how you will display the winning photos.
Share the link on your social channels or embed it on the contest page.

faqs.q: What information should a photo contest entry form collect?
faqs.a: The entrant's name and email, the category, the photo at full resolution, a title, and agreement to the entry terms. Where and when it was taken, and the story behind it, help judges too.

faqs.q: Do photo contest entrants keep the copyright?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Most contests ask only for permission to display the photo with credit, and the entry terms in this form say the photographer keeps copyright. Edit them to match your own rules.

faqs.q: Can under-18s enter a photo contest?
faqs.a: Many contests allow it with a parent or guardian's permission. This form asks for guardian details from anyone under 18 so you can confirm before shortlisting.

faqs.q: How do I stop ineligible entries?
faqs.a: Ask the eligibility question before the upload. Here, anyone who has composited their image is told it can't be entered before they spend time uploading it.
